name: Office application spawned a command interpreter
description: Lab rule 3 of 5. The 365 day window is a lab-only concession, because this lab ships historical data. A production deployment of this rule would use a short window and would alert on the shape of the traffic rather than on one address. A mail client or a spreadsheet starting a shell is the classic shape of a malicious document. This is the noisiest rule in the lab and almost everything it reports is a user who opened a macro-enabled attachment that they were expecting. No threshold is applied, so one event is one alert, which is deliberately unhelpful. The field is repeated on each side of every or rather than written in the shorter field:(a or b) form: Kibana's rule engine accepts both, but the Elasticsearch query behind the KQL bar does not, so the shorter spelling gives you a rule nobody can reproduce by hand in Discover.
query: (process.parent.name: "winword.exe" or process.parent.name: "excel.exe" or process.parent.name: "outlook.exe") and (process.name: "cmd.exe" or process.name: "powershell.exe" or process.name: "mshta.exe" or process.name: "wscript.exe")
